messages:
Sophia: Heads-up — CI perf job (multi-GPU comm/compute overlap) started failing after the NV graph capture change pushed yesterday. Repro on x2 A100, single sequence length profile. Error shows up inconsistently as stalls and some cudaGraphLaunch invalid-value errors.

Alex: ugh. saw a couple flaky reproductions locally. Do you have a minimal repro or logs? :thinking:

Sophia: Pasted the failing snippet from the CI log below. It's intermittent, but when it fails RT latency spikes to >200ms/token.
```
[worker0] kernel forward_layer_23 elapsed 0.12ms
[worker0] kv_prefetch queue enqueue
[worker0] cudaGraphLaunch returned cudaErrorInvalidValue
[worker1] allreduce start (NCCL)
[worker0] stall waiting for kv prefetch completion
```

Sophia: The code path changed to capture the forward pass with cudaStreamBeginCapture on the compute stream, while KV prefetch uses the dedicated copy stream and signals with events. I suspect capture + cross-stream events isn't being reproduced in the graph.

Raj: That matches my mental model — cudaGraph capture doesn't record event-based sync from other streams automatically. If the graph expects the prefetch event to have been signaled before launch, but the capture was scheduled without the event, the launch can race.

Alex: Is the sequence: 1) kick KV prefetch on copy stream, 2) record compute stream capture, 3) cudaGraphLaunch on compute stream? If capture happens before prefetch created the event, graph won't include the dependency.

Sophia: Exactly. In our old path we used explicit cudaStreamWaitEvent on the compute stream before running kernels, but the capture change removed the wait (thought safe since prefetch had been awaited earlier). The CI trace shows sometimes the wait wasn't registered into the graph.

Matt: Bisected to commit 8b7c2a1 — the change replaced runtime dispatch with cudaGraph capture to reduce launch overhead. Repro steps I used: run perf/job --profile=multi-gpu --seed=42 on 2 nodes, warmup 50 iters, then run 200 iterations. Failure rate ~30%.

Alex: Quick workaround: add a temporary cudaEventRecord on the copy stream and cudaStreamWaitEvent in the compute stream inside the capture region, so the event becomes part of the graph. That might serialize but should make it deterministic for CI.

Raj: Careful — if you create the event and record it before BeginCapture, the capture will record the wait as a dependency. But if the event is recorded after capture begins (or is external), it won't. We should either move prefetch so its event is signaled before we start capture, or delay BeginCapture until prefetch done for the batch head.

Sophia: Tried both: delaying BeginCapture until after prefetch reduces perf win (less capture coverage) but fixes flake. Recording event+wait inside capture fixed flake but reintroduces a small per-batch sync cost.

Matt: Perf numbers: baseline (no graph) = 1.0x; graph without fixes = 1.18x but 30% flake; graph with event-wait-in-capture = 1.14x stable. Might be acceptable as an interim.

Alex: Longer-term fix: update kernel selection / batch heuristics so prefetch happens deterministically before capture window, or extend the capture to include the prefetch on the copy stream (but graphs across streams are tricky and can't record external memcopy).

Raj: Another angle — use cudaGraphAddDependencies between graphs: build a subgraph for prefetch (on copy stream) and a compute graph, then add dependency from prefetch graph node to compute graph node so the runtime enforces ordering at launch. That requires constructing multi-node graph objects, but it's the clean solution.

Sophia: Good idea. Also found a profiler trace: nvprof shows compute stream kernels queued before copy stream completed; timeline has missing stream sync markers during capture periods. Screenshot attached in PR comment (internal).

infra-bot: Deploy notice: perf-ci/runner-17 rerun queued by @Sophia — https://ci.internal/retry/12345 :hammer:

Matt: I'm going to draft a small patch that does the record+wait inside capture for CI to get green, and a follow-up RFC for multi-graph dependency approach. Will open PR in a few hours.

Alex: If you need help with the NCCL ordering we can also add explicit barrier before the all-reduce when running under graph mode; NCCL sometimes assumes host-side ordering that graphs change.

Sophia: Thanks — ping me on the PR. Also adding a test harness that fuzzes prefetch timing to catch regressions. We should add that to perf-runner.

Raj: One more note: KV cache prefetch sometimes uses pinned host staging buffers; if those are moved into graph it might require different memcpys APIs (cudaMemcpyAsync vs captured memcpy). We'll need to audit that.

Sophia: Filing follow-ups: 1) hotfix PR with capture-event-wait (temp) 2) RFC for graph subgraphs + dependencies 3) perf test for prefetch timing variance.

Matt: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/482 (WIP)

Alex: :thumbsup:

Sophia: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread for traceability, will post final revert/merge notes when PR lands.
